comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's four reportable segments are Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded, each encompassing specific product lines for data centers, client devices, gaming hardware, and embedded solutions.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose their specific business segments and product focus in Item 1 to define their revenue streams. MU identifies the 'Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU)' as a primary reporting segment, highlighting its revenue performance and product mix (HBM, DDR, LPDDR, GDDR DRAM) for data center, PC, and graphics markets. Similarly, AMD defines four reportable segments—Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded—and details the specific product lines within the Data Center segment (AI accelerators, server CPUs, GPUs) and Client segment (CPUs, APUs). While MU focuses on a single named business unit's financial performance and product composition, AMD provides a structural definition of its multi-segment organizational model, establishing a comparable context for understanding their respective hardware-centric revenue drivers.
